sub_tasks.requirements: Both Variance-Exploding Stochastic Differential Equation (VESDE) and Variance-Preserving Stochastic Differential Equation (VPSDE) have been implemented following Appendix E.3
The forward noising process has been implemented following Section 2.2

verification.spec: Instantiate the forward noising SDE class with a small batch of theta_0 samples. Simulate the SDE for t in [0,T]. Verify that (a) at t near 0 the samples equal theta_0, (b) at t=T the marginal empirical mean and covariance are close to the stationary Gaussian (norm(mean)<0.2, ||cov - I||<0.3 for VP; VE reaches large-variance Gaussian), and (c) transition density gradient can be computed in closed form matching Song et al. (2021).

sub_tasks.requirements: VESDE has been implemented following Appendix E.3
The drift term for VESDE is defined as $f(x, t)=0$

verification.spec: Inspect the VESDE implementation: for any input x and t, verify the drift f(x,t) returns a zero tensor of the same shape as x.

sub_tasks.requirements: The diffusion term for VESDE is defined as $g(t)=\sigma_{min} \cdot (\frac{\sigma_{min}}{\sigma_{max}})^t \cdot \sqrt{2 \log \frac{\sigma_{max}}{\sigma_{min}}}$

verification.spec: Numerically evaluate the VESDE g(t) at several t values in [0,1] and compare against the closed-form sigma_min * (sigma_min/sigma_max)^t * sqrt(2*log(sigma_max/sigma_min)) using the code's sigma_min/sigma_max; assert element-wise match to <1e-5 relative error.

sub_tasks.requirements: The constant $\sigma_{\text{min}}$ for VESDE is set to 0.01 for the tasks SIR and Two Moons

verification.spec: Inspect the task-specific config or run script for SIR and Two Moons and verify sigma_min == 0.01 for the VESDE.

sub_tasks.requirements: The constant $\sigma_{\text{min}}$ for VESDE is set to 0.05 for the tasks Gaussian Linear, Gaussian Mixture, Gaussian Linear Uniform, Bernoulli GLM, SLCP, and Lotka Volterra

verification.spec: Inspect the task-specific configs for Gaussian Linear, Gaussian Mixture, Gaussian Linear Uniform, Bernoulli GLM, SLCP, and Lotka Volterra and verify sigma_min == 0.05 for the VESDE in each.

sub_tasks.requirements: The constant $\sigma_{\text{max}}$ for VESDE is chosen to be as large as the maximum Euclidean distance between all pairs of training data points for the current task. For sequential methods, the training data points that are used are the training data points available in the first round

verification.spec: For a given task, load the first-round training theta dataset and compute the maximum pairwise Euclidean distance D. Then load the sigma_max hyperparameter used by the VESDE for that task. Assert |sigma_max - D| / D < 0.05 (i.e., sigma_max equals max pairwise distance of first-round training data).

sub_tasks.requirements: The time interval used in VESDE is (0, 1]

verification.spec: Inspect the VESDE class configuration: assert t_min > 0 (e.g., 1e-5 or similar small positive) and t_max == 1.0, matching the time interval (0, 1].

sub_tasks.requirements: VPSDE has been implemented following Appendix E.3
The drift term for VPSDE is defined as $f(x, t)=-\frac{1}{2}\beta_t\theta_t$, where $\beta_t = \beta_{\text{min}} + t(\beta_{\text{max}} - \beta_{\text{min}})$

verification.spec: Instantiate the VPSDE class with configured beta_min, beta_max. For random theta_t and multiple t in [0,1], compute f(theta_t, t) via the class's drift method and compare against reference value -0.5 * (beta_min + t*(beta_max - beta_min)) * theta_t elementwise. Assert max relative error < 1e-5.

sub_tasks.requirements: The diffusion term for VPSDE is defined as $\sqrt{\beta_t}$, where $\beta_t = \beta_{\text{min}} + t(\beta_{\text{max}} - \beta_{\text{min}})$

verification.spec: Instantiate the VPSDE class. For multiple t in [0,1], compute g(t) via its diffusion method and compare against sqrt(beta_min + t*(beta_max - beta_min)). Assert max relative error < 1e-5.

sub_tasks.requirements: The constant $\beta_\text{min}$ for VPSDE is set to 0.1

verification.spec: Inspect the VPSDE configuration/constructor and verify that beta_min == 0.1.

sub_tasks.requirements: The constant $\beta_\text{max}$ for VPSDE is set to 11.0

verification.spec: Inspect the VPSDE configuration/constructor and verify that beta_max == 11.0.

sub_tasks.requirements: The time interval used in VPSDE is (0, 1]

verification.spec: Inspect the VPSDE class configuration: assert t_min > 0 (small positive epsilon) and t_max == 1.0.

sub_tasks.requirements: Both VESDE and VPSDE have implemented code to compute the (gradients of the) transition log density
Code has been implemented for VESDE to compute the (gradients of the) transition log density

verification.spec: For VESDE, sample many theta_t ~ p_{t|0}(theta_t | theta_0) via ancestral sampling of the forward SDE and via the closed-form transition; compare empirical mean/cov to the analytic mean/cov (theta_0 and sigma^2(t) I). Also verify that grad_{theta_t} log p_{t|0}(theta_t | theta_0) computed by the code equals -(theta_t - theta_0)/sigma^2(t) up to <1e-5 relative error.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented for VPSDE to compute the (gradients of the) transition log density

verification.spec: For VPSDE, verify closed-form transition density: sample theta_t via forward SDE integration and compare empirical mean/covariance to alpha(t)*theta_0 and (1-alpha(t)^2) I where alpha(t)=exp(-0.5*int_0^t beta_s ds). Verify grad log p_{t|0}(theta_t|theta_0) returned by code matches -(theta_t - alpha(t) theta_0)/(1-alpha(t)^2) within 1e-5.

sub_tasks.requirements: Neural Posterior Score Estimation (NPSE) has been implemented
A neural network is trained to approximate the sequence of score functions $\nabla_\theta \log p_t(\theta_t \mid x)$ of the (perturbed) posterior distributions
When training NPSE, for each sampled parameter from the prior $\theta_0$, code is implemented to use the simulator to generate a corresponding observation $x$; $x \sim p(x|theta_0)$

verification.spec: Instantiate an sbibm task simulator. Draw theta_0 from prior, call the training-data generation code that produces (theta, x) pairs. Assert that x for each theta was produced by invoking the task's simulator (compare shape/dtype and, using a deterministic-seeded task, exact values against direct simulator(theta_0) call).

sub_tasks.requirements: When training NPSE, for each $\theta_0$ and corresponding observation $x$, code is implemented to simulate the forward diffusion process using an SDE to obtain $\theta_t$ at time $t$

verification.spec: Given (theta_0, x) pairs, call the code path that samples theta_t. Fix a t in (0,1] and repeatedly sample theta_t | theta_0. Verify the empirical mean/covariance match the SDE's closed-form p_{t|0}(theta_t | theta_0) (VP or VE) within 5% relative error.

sub_tasks.requirements: When training NPSE, code is implemented to compute the loss as a Monte Carlo estimate of $\left\| s_\psi(\theta_t, x, t) - \nabla_{\theta_t} \log p_t(\theta_t | \theta) \right\|^2$, where $s_\psi(\theta_t, x, t)$ is the result of the score network, and $\nabla_{\theta_t} \log p_{t \mid 0}(\theta_t \mid \theta_0)$ is the forward diffusion transition log density

verification.spec: Instantiate the NPSE trainer's loss function on a small synthetic batch of (theta_0, x) pairs with known forward transition p_{t|0} (Gaussian). Numerically compute the DSM loss ||s_psi(theta_t,x,t) - grad_theta_t log p_{t|0}(theta_t|theta_0)||^2 (weighted by lambda_t and averaged over t and batch) via a straightforward reference implementation and confirm it matches the code's loss to <1e-5.

sub_tasks.requirements: Approximate samples can be generated from the target posterior distribution using the neural network
When sampling using NPSE, samples are drawn from the stationary distribution $\pi$ (unit gaussian distribution); $\overline{\theta}_0 \sim \pi(\cdot)$

verification.spec: Invoke the NPSE posterior sampling function. Intercept or inspect the initial state drawn: assert the initial samples are drawn from a standard multivariate Gaussian (N(0,I)) of dimensionality d. Test with a batch of 10000 samples: assert ||empirical_mean|| < 0.05 and ||empirical_cov - I||_F / sqrt(d) < 0.05.

sub_tasks.requirements: When sampling using NPSE, the approximation of the time-reversal of the probability flow ODE is implemented given some observation $x = x_{\text{obs}}$, and replacing the score of the (perturbed) posterior(s) with the neural network; $\nabla_\theta \log p_t(\theta \vert x_{\text{obs}}) \approx s_\psi(\theta_t, x_{\text{obs}}, t)$. RK45 is used to solve the ODE

verification.spec: Given a trained (or dummy) score network, verify the NPSE sampler implements the probability-flow ODE (Eq. 4) integrated backward in time from t=T to t=0 with drift [f(theta,t) - 0.5*g(t)^2 * s_psi(theta,x_obs,t)], starting from pi (standard Gaussian) samples. Substitute a known analytic score (e.g., for a Gaussian target) and confirm returned samples match target distribution moments within 5%.

sub_tasks.requirements: Truncated SNPSE (TSNPSE) has been implemented
In TSNPSE, given a total budget of $N$ simulations and $R$ rounds, the simulations are evenly distributed across rounds; the number of simulations per round $M$ is computed as $M=N/R$

verification.spec: Call TSNPSE with N=1000, R=5. Instrument the training loop to record simulations per round. Assert each round used exactly N/R = 200 simulations, and total simulations = N.

sub_tasks.requirements: In TSNPSE, the proposal prior in the $r$-th round is correctly computed
In TSNPSE, the initial proposal prior is equivalent to the known prior of the current task; $p(\theta) =: p^{-0}(\theta)$

verification.spec: Instantiate TSNPSE with a known prior. Before any training rounds execute, inspect the internal proposal_priors list / initial p_bar^0. Draw a large batch (1e5) from it and compare its empirical histogram / log_prob values with the task's prior; assert KS distance across each dim < 0.02.

sub_tasks.requirements: In TSNPSE, all subsequent proposal priors are correctly computed

In TSNPSE, in the $r$-th round, after applying the NPSE algorithm to learn a score network, 20000 samples are simulated from the approximate posterior via (the time-reversal of) the probability flow ODE using the neural network approximation of $\nabla_\theta \log p_t(\theta \vert x_{\text{obs}})$

verification.spec: Run TSNPSE for one round on a small task. Inspect the code path that constructs bar_p^r: verify that exactly 20000 samples are drawn from p_psi(theta|x_obs) via integration of the probability-flow ODE (reverse time) using the trained score network at x=x_obs, before HPR truncation.

sub_tasks.requirements: In TSNPSE, in the $r$-th round, the (approximate) likelihood $p(\theta \mid x_{\text{obs}})$ of the samples under the model is computed using the instantaneous-change-of-variables formula

verification.spec: Call the density-evaluation function used by TSNPSE for a batch of theta samples. Verify the implementation integrates d/dt log p_t = -Tr[grad_theta(f - 0.5 g^2 s_psi)] along the probability-flow ODE (equation 5) between t=0 and t=T, and returns log p_0(theta|x_obs). Compare against a manual Hutchinson-trace reimplementation on random theta; assert per-sample log-density agreement within 1e-2.

sub_tasks.requirements: In TSNPSE, in the $r$-th round, the truncation boundary is computed as the $\epsilon = 5 \times 10^{-4}$-th percentile of the samples from the approximate posterior. This defines the log-probability rejection threshold for rejection sampling.

verification.spec: In TSNPSE, invoke the routine that computes the truncation threshold. Given the 20000 samples from the approximate posterior and their log-probabilities under p_psi, assert threshold = np.quantile(log_probs, 5e-4) within numerical tolerance. Verify epsilon = 5e-4 is used as a config constant.

sub_tasks.requirements: In TSNPSE, in the $r$-th round, sampling from the truncated proposal prior is correctly implemented
In TSNPSE, in the $r$-th round, when sampling from the truncated proposal prior, samples are first drawn from the prior as $\theta \sim p(\theta)$.

verification.spec: Call the truncated-proposal sampling function. Instrument or inspect the code: verify the first step draws candidate samples from the task's prior p(theta) via prior.sample(). E.g. patch prior.sample and confirm it is called before any rejection/acceptance step.

sub_tasks.requirements: In TSNPSE, in the $r$-th round, when sampling from the truncated proposal prior, an initial rejection step is applied to samples drawn from the prior; the samples are rejected if they do not belong to the empirical hyperrectangle defined by the approximate posterior samples. That is, the hyperrectangle defined as the Cartesian product of the one-dimensional intervals with endpoints given by the minimum and maximum of the approximate posterior samples in each dimension.

verification.spec: In the truncated proposal sampler, verify that after drawing candidate theta ~ prior, an initial rejection step tests membership in the axis-aligned hyperrectangle defined by componentwise min/max of the 20000 approximate-posterior samples. Test: construct a fake posterior sample cloud within a known box, generate prior samples, and confirm all accepted candidates lie within that empirical hyperrectangle.

sub_tasks.requirements: In TSNPSE, in the $r$-th round, when sampling from the truncated proposal prior, following the initial rejection step, the likelihood of the samples from the prior under the approximate posterior is computed using the instantaneous change-of-variables formula.

verification.spec: Inspect the TSNPSE truncated-proposal sampling code: verify that when computing the likelihood/density of prior samples under the approximate posterior for the acceptance test, it invokes the instantaneous change-of-variables formula (Eq. 5) applied to the probability flow ODE (Eq. 4), e.g., via a CNF log-prob call using the trace of the Jacobian of the ODE drift.

sub_tasks.requirements: In TSNPSE, in the $r$-th round, when sampling from the truncated proposal prior, samples are accepted if the likelihood under the approximation posterior is greater than the truncation boundary that has been computed on the $r$-th round. Otherwise they are rejected.

verification.spec: Construct a mock approximate posterior with a known density and a known truncation boundary. Feed samples with densities both above and below the boundary to the TSNPSE rejection routine; assert samples with density > boundary are accepted and those below are rejected.

sub_tasks.requirements: In TSNPSE, in the $r$-th round, when sampling from the truncated proposal prior, the previous steps are repeated until the required number of samples from the proposal prior have been obtained.

verification.spec: Call the TSNPSE truncated-proposal sampler with a target N and check that (a) the returned tensor has exactly N accepted samples and (b) the routine loops (draw → accept/reject) until N is reached rather than returning fewer samples.

sub_tasks.requirements: In TSNPSE, in the $r$-th round, a dataset $\mathcal{D}$ of $|M|$ samples is constructed by drawing $\theta_i \sim {p}^{-r-1}(\theta)$, $x_i \sim p(x \mid \theta_i)$, and adding $(\theta_i, x_i)$ to $\mathcal{D}$, where ${p}^{-r-1}(\theta)$ denotes the proposal prior and $p(x|\theta)$ denotes the simulator.

verification.spec: Run TSNPSE for one round on a toy task; assert that in each round r, the code draws exactly M parameter samples from the truncated proposal p^{r-1}, simulates x_i ~ p(x|theta_i), and appends the resulting (theta_i, x_i) pairs to dataset D so that |D| grows by exactly M per round.

sub_tasks.requirements: In TSNPSE, in each of the rounds, given a dataset $\mathcal{D}$ of $|M|$ samples, the NPSE algorithm is followed to learn a neural network which approximates the score(s) of the perturbed posterior(s) $\nabla_{\theta_t} \log p_t(\theta_t | x)$

verification.spec: In each TSNPSE round, verify that the training step minimizes a Monte Carlo estimate of the TSNPSE-DSM loss (Eq. 11) over dataset D and produces a score network s_psi(theta_t, x, t) approximating ∇_theta log p_t(theta_t|x). Check on a Gaussian toy where the analytic score is known: after training, MSE between s_psi and the true score is small (e.g., < 0.1) at multiple t values.

sub_tasks.requirements: In TSNPSE, the score network computed in the final round is used as the final approximation of the scores $\nabla_{\theta_t} \log p_t(\theta_t | x)$, and can be used to generate approximate samples from the posterior, as per the standard NPSE algorithm

verification.spec: Run TSNPSE for R rounds and confirm that the returned posterior sampler uses the score network from the final round (round R) plugged into the reverse-time SDE/probability-flow ODE (Eq. 4). Check by comparing sampler outputs to samples generated using the same final network manually inserted into the ODE — they should match.
